content:
As the finale of iFixit's teardown of Apple's September new products, iFixit has today published its teardown report on the new-generation Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Here's what they found.

iFixit Tears Down Apple Watch Ultra 4

After heating the display of the new Apple Watch Ultra 4, iFixit's Shahram Mokhtari pried open the screen using the company's new metal pick, revealing the battery and Taptic Engine.

He noted that replacing the 2.444 Wh battery (compared to the 2.313 Wh in the Ultra 3) still requires removing the display first, and this remains a major flaw in repair convenience. The four screws on the back housing only provide access to the sensor assembly and the device's S11 chip.

However, once the display adhesive is cleared, removing the battery and the press-fit connector for the display appear relatively straightforward, provided the first step is done carefully enough to avoid cutting any of the cables beneath.

That said, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 has shown no notable improvement in repair convenience, earning the same 4/10 score from iFixit as the previous generation.

iFixit Tears Down Apple Watch Series 12

iFixit's teardown of the new Apple Watch Series 12 shows a slight improvement in repair convenience, with Apple having added stretch-release adhesive and pull tabs, making the 1.461 Wh battery (compared to the 1.403 Wh in the 46mm Series 11) easier to remove.

However, as with the Apple Watch Ultra 4, getting inside the Series 12 still requires prying off the firmly glued display first, and this remains the biggest obstacle to repair. Mokhtari pointed out that the tolerances around the Series 12 display are even tighter than on the Ultra 4, requiring so much force that he was worried about breaking the screen.

Mokhtari also mentioned that Apple has replaced the ZIF connector and adhesive tape previously used for the display with a simpler press-fit connector.

The trade-off is that replacing the screen now also requires removing and replacing the battery at the same time. "But once you've gone that far, why not just do it while you're at it?" he added.

Overall, these modest improvements in repair convenience were enough for iFixit to give the Series 12 a repair score of 4/10, which is 1 point higher than the basic Apple Watch model they previously scored.

As a comparison, iFixit gave Google's Pixel Watch 5 a repair score of 9/10, noting that the watch's display can be removed with just two Torx screws and a waterproof gasket, and the battery does not require dealing with adhesive.
